ceramic.snippet: Q&A Summary How do you respond to investors who view the CEO transition timing as concerning amid subdued sales and lower new store productivity? Tom Taylor said he is not going anywhere and will partner with Brad Paulsen as Executive Chair, citing a proven track record and strong team. The company understands what a trough looks like, has a good store class for next year with lower costs, and is pivoting to mid- and top-tier markets for the 2026 class. What could the comp look like in a hypothetical 3% to 4% existing home sales environment in 2026, given new store waterfall benefits but home price pressure in Texas and Florida? It is too early to discuss 2026, but if existing home sales comp positive, the company has a good ability to comp positive. New stores still provide a waterfall benefit (less than years ago), each recent class is comping positive, and nearly 50% of stores are less than five years old. How can the slowdown be attributed to a contracting industry versus competition? It is much more a contracting industry issue; across publicly reported flooring retailers and manufacturers, everyone has been in a negative environment while Floor & Decors total growth has been positive. Recent classes opened in smaller, declining markets, and competitors appear to be doing worse. Why are comparable store sales degrading rather than benefiting from independent and regional closures? Management does not believe comps are getting much worse; the company is bouncing along the bottom and doing better than peers given its over 5% total growth. On a two-year stack, every quarter is sequentially improving (Q1 -13.3%, Q2 -8.6%, Q3 -7.6%), and product margin was up 80 basis points year over year. Can you quantify price changes and the consumer response? The company has taken modest price increases through the year.

Construction Partners reported fiscal Q3 results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, with revenue of $999.4 million and net income of $59.6 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $163.0 million and adjusted diluted EPS on an adjusted net income basis was $1.08 for the quarter. The company said backlog reached a record $3.36 billion and raised its fiscal 2026 guidance across revenue, net income and Adjusted EBITDA.

**Financial Highlights**

- Revenue: $999.4 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 (up 28.2% year-over-year from $779.3 million).
- Gross profit: $168.4 million for the quarter (compare to $131.8 million in Q3 FY25).
- Operating income: $109.4 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.
- Net income: $59.6 million for the quarter; diluted net income per share $1.06.
- Adjusted metrics: Adjusted net income $60.6 million (adjusted diluted EPS $1.08) and Adjusted EBITDA $163.0 million; Adjusted EBITDA margin 16.3% for the quarter.

**Business Highlights**

- Backlog reached a record $3.36 billion at June 30, 2026, up from $2.94 billion at June 30, 2025 and $3.14 billion at March 31, 2026, providing visibility into future work.
- Company expanded its Oklahoma footprint with the acquisition of Ellsworth Construction, enhancing presence in Tulsa and Oklahoma City and expanding data center construction capabilities.
- Management cited resilient decentralized operating model and healthy demand for public infrastructure and commercial construction across Sunbelt markets despite energy cost inflation and wet weather in May.
- Raised fiscal 2026 outlook: revenue now guided to $3.640B–$3.680B; net income $165.0M–$168.0M; Adjusted net income $177.6M–$181.4M; Adjusted EBITDA $559.0M–$569.0M with Adjusted EBITDA margin 15.36%–15.46%.
